name: Plyometric Push-Up
description: The plyometric push-up is an explosive upper body press variation in which the athlete pushes off with enough force to leave the ground, optionally clapping between repetitions. It trains the stretch-shortening cycle of the pectoral muscles and triceps, developing explosive upper body pushing power. The exercise is a staple of athletic conditioning programs targeting sport-specific upper body force production.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a standard push-up position — hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, body in a straight line from head to heels.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. Ensure adequate floor space and a non-slip surface.
steps: Step 1: Begin in push-up position with the body in a straight plank line.
Step 2: Lower the chest to the floor under control.
Step 3: Press explosively with maximum effort — drive the hands into the floor to generate enough force to lift the hands off the ground.
Step 4: Optionally clap while airborne, then catch the fall by landing with slightly bent elbows.
Step 5: Absorb the landing and immediately lower into the next repetition.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent. Exhale sharply and forcefully at the moment of push-off.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag — the body must remain rigid throughout
Insufficient pressing force — the hands must fully leave the ground
Catching with locked elbows — this places severe strain on the elbow joint
safety_considerations: Master standard push-ups before attempting plyometric variations.
Land with soft elbows, never locked out.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up depth — chest to floor or near it. Full extension (hands off ground) at top.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Maximum effort on each rep. 5–10 reps per set for power. Rest fully between sets.
coaching_cues: Push the floor away as hard as possible
Tight core throughout — no hip sag
Catch soft — bend the elbows on landing
